description: (0.5.0) Durable cursors and retention (RFC-ACDP-0018 §5.4, overriding RFC-ACDP-0005 §2.5.4's one-hour bound for /changes). Behavioral, registry-side.

input.setup: A cursor C1 obtained at t0.

expected.behavior: C1 still works at t0 + 2 h and at t0 + 29 d.
A cursor pointing before the oldest retained entry fails; consumer must resync (§7).
capabilities.limits carries change_retention_seconds >= 2592000, max_change_filters >= 100 and max_changes_page >= 100.

scenarios.name: E — issued cursor the registry can no longer place

expected.behavior: Self-test (black-box testing cannot rotate a registry's cursor key): obtain a cursor, rotate the cursor-protection key (or otherwise rebuild the feed), then poll with the old cursor. The registry answers cursor_expired, not invalid_cursor, because it issued that cursor (RFC-ACDP-0018 §5.4). invalid_cursor stays reserved for scenario C's unparseable or forged input.

scenarios.name: F — cursors from before a sequence reset

expected.behavior: Self-test: obtain cursors at several positions, restore the feed from a backup that predates some served entries (so seq values will be reused), then poll with each pre-restore cursor, including one beyond the restored head. Every pre-restore cursor is refused with cursor_expired; none is honoured, so no consumer can silently skip the entries that reuse its numbers (RFC-ACDP-0018 §5.3).
